How the game works

Every player is classified.
Every team is balanced.

Each player is rated from 1.0 to 5.0 depending on trunk control and function — 1.0 for those most impaired, 5.0 for the least. A 5.0 can be an able-bodied player: they play too. It's not a ranking of skill. It's what makes the line-up fair.

  • When playing in domestic leagues, the five players a team fields can never total more than 14.5 points combined
  • A low-point player and a high-point player are equally valuable on court
  • It's the rule that lets a first-season player and a national-squad player share a line-up

Get involved

Training is open to anyone

You don't need a sports chair, an impairment or any experience to join us. We provide chairs, qualified coaches run every session, and the only stupid question is the one you didn't ask.

Beginners

First session

Come along, borrow a chair, learn the basics of pushing, pivoting and passing. No commitment, no pressure.

Membership

Come and play

Whoever you are, whatever your skill level or ability — young players, experienced players, first-timers and internationals all train together. We take the basketball seriously, but 30 years on we're still first and foremost a family: welcoming, fun, and here for each other. You don't need your own chair to start.

Jags in the community

Basketball that brings people together

For over 20 years, Jaguars coaches have taken wheelchair basketball into schools and workplaces — delivering inclusive sports sessions and team building that put everyone on a level playing field.

Schools

Wheelchair basketball in schools

Students of all abilities play together — building teamwork, communication, resilience and confidence, while developing strength and coordination. It's a real leveller, and a powerful way to grow disability sport awareness.

Team building

Sessions for any group

We've run sessions for groups of 6 to over 60, and mini-tournaments from 4 to 16 teams. Even the self-declared "not sporty" come away wanting another go — a genuinely inclusive way to bring a whole organisation together.

"It was such a memorable experience for children and staff alike. Great to see so many pupils who are usually less enthusiastic about sport completely engrossed — playing with a smile on their faces."
David Morris
Y6 Teacher & PE Coordinator, St Johns Primary Academy
